title: The Spirit of truth (John 16:12–15)
hookLine: I have many things to say but you cannot bear them now

lines: NOT THE WHOLE CHART AT ONCE.
cards: A good doctor doesn't read you the whole chart in the first five minutes. A good parent doesn't explain everything about death to a four-year-old at bedtime.

A good teacher doesn't start calculus on the first day of algebra. Not because they're hiding something, but because there's an order to understanding. Some things you can only carry when you're ready.
Jesus has just told his friends he gave them everything he heard from the Father. Now, still at the table, he says something that sounds like the opposite.

teach.b: In the Douay-Rheims: "I have yet many things to say to you: but you cannot bear them now. But when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will teach you all truth." So which is it? Has he told them everything, or not?
Both, in a way. Everything has been given in him, but they can't carry it all yet. Bear is a carrying word, the kind you'd use for a heavy load.
It's honest about the disciples: men who, within hours, will fall asleep in the garden and run. Jesus doesn't pretend they're ready.

teach.h: HE WILL GUIDE YOU INTO ALL TRUTH.
teach.b: So he promises the Spirit of truth, who will teach them, or in the Greek, guide them, lead them along the way, into all the truth. Not dump it on them. Walk them into it.
And the Spirit, Jesus says, won't bring a new message of his own.

teach.h: NOT NEW: WHAT IS MINE, SHOWN.
teach.b: He'll take what is mine and show it to you. Catholics hear in this promise the Church's long, slow understanding of what it received.
The Second Vatican Council taught that the understanding of what has been handed down grows over time, through contemplation, study and the experience of believers.

teach.h: NEWMAN: DOCTRINE GROWS LIKE A LIFE.
teach.b: In the nineteenth century John Henry Newman, now a canonized saint, wrote a whole book on how doctrine develops, the way a living thing grows up without turning into something else.
Not new revelation, the Church says, but deeper understanding of what was given. Not yet, but coming.

how: Catholics pray to the Holy Spirit for understanding, especially at Pentecost and before study or decisions, often with the traditional prayer "Come, Holy Spirit."

what everyone must grasp all at once

games.q: you're Jesus at the supper. your friends are exhausted and frightened, and there's much more they need to know. what do you do?
o: tell them all of it now, while there's time.
tell them they can't bear it now, and promise the Spirit.
games.why: I have yet many things to say to you: but you cannot bear them now. the Spirit of truth will lead them into it.

practice: Bring to mind one thing you don't understand yet, about your faith, your life, a person, a loss, and don't try to solve it. Imagine setting it on a table in front of you: not thrown away, just set down to come back to later.
If you pray, leave it there with Jesus's promise, he will teach you all truth; if you don't, simply let it rest on the table.

wordCard.voice: Truth. Jesus's promise that the Spirit will guide his friends into the truth they can't yet carry. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: not yet, but coming. Some things wait until you can carry them. Day five hundred twenty-three, done.
